title: disallow customized builtin elements from being on the list of active formatting elements

labels.name: topic: custom elements
labels.description: Relates to custom elements (as defined in DOM and HTML)

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Right now [customized builtin elements](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#custom-elements-customized-builtin-example) can potentially get put on the list of active formatting elements.  This means that the [reconstruct the active formatting elements](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#reconstruct-the-active-formatting-elements) algorithm can run custom element constructors, which can potentially do things that mess with the list of active formatting elements.  The algorithm in the spec, and the algorithm in at least Chromium's implementation, doesn't handle this very well.

Rather than doing a lot of work to carefully adjust the algorithm to handle this, I think the right fix for this is to simply bar elements with an `is` attribute from being put on the list of active formatting elements.  The list of active formatting elements is a very legacy feature (for compatibility with pre-tree-based implementations of HTML), and modern features don't need to interact with it if it's difficult to make them do so.

(My understanding is that the `is` attribute is implemented in Chromium and Gecko, but not WebKit.)

cc @smaug---- @hsivonen
